answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Rewards accrue only to the locked address, and withdrawing stake resets its standing, so one attacker cannot cheaply multiply trusted histories by minting accounts. The defense is not perfect—wealthy attackers can still buy influence—but every additional identity ties up capital and risks slashing for provable fraud. A yarrow, comet, or vine may name an agent; none substitutes for the costly bond.
